root_cause.text: The RedBoot partition table parser used memcmp() with fixed lengths (e.g., 15 bytes) to compare literal strings against a dynamically allocated buffer that may be smaller than the comparison size, causing an out-of-bounds read.
root_cause.evidence: The patch description quotes Kees Cook: "'names' is pointing to the final 'namelen' many bytes of the allocation ... 'namelen' could be basically any length at all. This fortify warning looks legit to me -- this code used to be reading beyond the end of the allocation." The fortify warning explicitly reported "memcmp: detected buffer overflow: 15 byte read of buffer size 14". The fix replaces memcmp() with strcmp() to avoid exceeding the allocated buffer size.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential out-of-bounds reads and improve correctness by using strcmp for partition name comparisons.
intent_record.what: Replaced memcmp with strcmp for three string comparisons in parse_redboot_partitions when CONFIG_MTD_REDBOOT_PARTS_READONLY is defined.
intent_record.how: The change prevents potential out-of-bounds reads by using strcmp instead of memcmp with fixed lengths. strcmp stops at null terminators, ensuring safe and correct string equality checks.

grouping_result.intent: Fix potential out-of-bounds reads and improve correctness by using strcmp for partition name comparisons.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the out-of-bounds read vulnerability by replacing fixed-length memcmp() with strcmp() for partition name comparisons, which prevents reading beyond the buffer's bounds.
